paper.title: CRIMED: Lower and Upper Bounds on Regret for Bandits with Unbounded Stochastic Corruption

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with unbounded stochastic corruption, general arm family L (lower bound)
unmapped: Huber contamination: each observation is replaced with probability epsilon in (0,1/2) by a sample from an arbitrary (possibly unbounded, time-varying) corruption distribution H_{a,n}; no corruption budget C
corruption probability epsilon is known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: with a fixed $\varepsilon\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, the agent observes a sample from the chosen arm's distribution with probability $1-\varepsilon$, or from an arbitrary corruption distribution with probability $\varepsilon$. Importantly, we impose no assumptions on these corruption distributions, which can be unbounded.

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian bandits (unit variance) with unbounded stochastic corruption
unmapped: Huber contamination: each observation is replaced with probability epsilon in (0,1/2) by a sample from an arbitrary (possibly unbounded, time-varying) corruption distribution; no corruption budget C
corruption probability epsilon is known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: When $\cal L = \cal G$, the collection of all Gaussian distributions with a unit variance ... the algorithm observes $Y_n \sim \mu_{A_n}$ with probability $1-\varepsilon$, and with probability $\varepsilon$, it observes a sample from an arbitrary distribution $H_{A_n,n}$.

symbols.KLeps_inf_a: corrupted KL-inf: min over kappa in L with mean >= m*(mu) and corruptions H,H' of KL((1-eps)mu_a+eps H, (1-eps)kappa+eps H')

conditions: bound on sup over corruption distributions of E[N_a(T)] for each suboptimal arm a

source.label: lem:lower_bound
source.quote: For $\varepsilon > 0$, $\mathcal L \subset \mathcal P(\R)$, and a bandit instance $\mu\in\mathcal L^K$, for any suboptimal arm $a$ in $\mu$, a uniformly-good algorithm satisfies \[ \liminf\limits_{T\rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{\log T}\lrp{\sup\limits_{{\bf H} \in\mathcal{P}(\R)^{K}}\Exp{\mu \corby {\bf H}}{N_a(T)}} \ge~\frac{1}{\eKinf(\mu_a,m^*(\mu); \mathcal{L})}. \]

results.notes: Bound is on expected number of pulls of suboptimal arm a (worst case over corruption), not regret directly; regret = sum_a E[N_a]Delta_a. Uniformly-good is defined w.r.t. all corruption sequences.

symbols.kleps_G_a: corrupted Gaussian divergence kl^eps_G(m(mu_a), m*(mu)) = min_{H,H'} KL(N(m_a,1) corrupted by H, N(m*,1) corrupted by H')

source.label: th:lower_bound_gauss
source.quote: For $\mu\in\mathcal \cG^K$, any uniformly-good algorithm satisfies for any suboptimal arm $a$ \[ \liminf\limits_{T\rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{\log (T)} \left(\sup\limits_{{\bf H} \in\mathcal{P}(\R)^K}\Exp{\mu \corby {\bf H}}{N_a(T)}\right)~\ge~\frac{1}{\ekl_\cG(m(\mu_a),m^*(\mu))}~\]

results.notes: Bound on pull counts of suboptimal arm. kl^eps_G is zero (bound infinite) when Delta_a <= 2 Phi^{-1}(1/(2(1-eps))).

symbols.delta_T: delta with delta^2 = 1/log(1+log(1+log T)) (analysis parameter, not a failure probability)
symbols.N_min: forced exploration length, ceil(2 log T log(1+log(1+log T))^2 s_eps^2 / log(1+log(T)^0.99))

conditions: for each suboptimal arm a, Delta_a > 2*Phi^{-1}(1/(2(1-eps)))

source.label: th:upper_bound
source.quote: For $\varepsilon \in (0,\frac{1}{2})$ and $\mu\in\cG^K$ such that for each suboptimal arm $a$, $\Delta_a >\Delta_{\min}$, \rimed{} satisfies \[ \E[N_a(T)] \le N_{\min} +  \frac{\log(T)}{ \ekl_\cG\lrp{m(\mu_{a}), m^*(\mu)}-2\delta\left(\Delta_a + \delta + \Delta_{\min}\right)} + O((\log T)^{0.99}),\] where $m^*(\mu)=\max_a m(\mu_a)$, and $\delta^2:=\lrp{\log(1+\log(1+\log T))}^{-1}$.

results.notes: Bound on expected pulls of suboptimal arm a (regret = sum Delta_a E[N_a]). Only the last term is O((log T)^0.99); first two terms are explicit, notation O used for the whole expression. Paper's Delta_min is not the smallest gap; renamed Delta_eps. Delta_i stands for Delta_a. Exact finite term in Eq. (finite_ub).

conditions: for each suboptimal arm a, Delta_a > 2*Phi^{-1}(1/(2(1-eps)))

source.quote: For $\varepsilon\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$ and $\mu \in \cG^K$ such that for each suboptimal arm $a$, $\Delta_a > \Delta_{\min}$, \rimed{} is asymptotically optimal, i.e., $\limsup\limits_{T\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\E\lrs{N_a(T)}}{\log T} \le \frac{1}{\ekl_{\cG}(m(\mu_a), m^*(\mu))}. $

results.notes: Matches Proposition 2 lower bound. Pull-count bound per suboptimal arm.
